description: Positive vs negative affect. Linearly encoded in language models by a large literature; if a tight pair cannot recover this, tightening is what broke the probe.
positive_en: He was delighted with the result
She felt cheerful about the news from home
The evening left him happy and light
They were pleased with how the meeting went
He described the outcome as wonderful
The letter made her glad for the rest of the week
negative_en: He was disappointed with the result
She felt gloomy about the news from home
The evening left him miserable and heavy
They were annoyed with how the meeting went
He described the outcome as dreadful
The letter made her sad for the rest of the week

description: Whether the sentence asserts or denies. A single word changes, so overlap is near total; if the probe cannot find this, nothing tight can be found.
positive_en: He did come to the meeting on time
She has read the report already
They were able to reach the office before noon
The shop was open when he arrived
He remembered to send the documents
The road was clear on the way back
negative_en: He did not come to the meeting on time
She has not read the report already
They were not able to reach the office before noon
The shop was not open when he arrived
He did not remember to send the documents
The road was not clear on the way back

description: Past vs future reference, holding the event fixed. Grammatical rather than semantic, and a standard probe target.
positive_en: He travelled to the coast last week
She finished the report yesterday morning
They moved into the new house last spring
The company hired him three months ago
He sold the car before the holiday
The rain stopped an hour ago
negative_en: He will travel to the coast next week
She will finish the report tomorrow morning
They will move into the new house next spring
The company will hire him three months from now
He will sell the car before the holiday
The rain will stop in an hour

description: First person vs third person, holding the event and wording fixed. If a probe cannot separate this it is not separating anything.
positive_en: I opened the shop at seven every morning
I waited for the bus in the rain
I paid the bill before leaving the table
I found the keys under the newspaper
I answered the letter the same evening
I locked the door behind me
negative_en: He opened the shop at seven every morning
He waited for the bus in the rain
He paid the bill before leaving the table
He found the keys under the newspaper
He answered the letter the same evening
He locked the door behind me

description: The same single-word valence contrast at twice the sample size. Valence at n=6 came out at chance while structural controls came out at ceiling, which points at power rather than absence: a single evaluative word in an otherwise identical frame is a small share of a mean-pooled sentence. If doubling n recovers it, the concept result is a power limit of this design, not evidence that the concepts are unrepresented.
positive_en: He was delighted with the result
She felt cheerful about the news from home
The evening left him happy and light
They were pleased with how the meeting went
He described the outcome as wonderful
The letter made her glad for the rest of the week
He was thrilled by the decision
She sounded joyful on the telephone
The visit left them content and rested
He called the arrangement excellent
The report was encouraging from the first page
She was relieved by what she heard
negative_en: He was disappointed with the result
She felt gloomy about the news from home
The evening left him miserable and heavy
They were annoyed with how the meeting went
He described the outcome as dreadful
The letter made her sad for the rest of the week
He was dismayed by the decision
She sounded mournful on the telephone
The visit left them weary and drained
He called the arrangement terrible
The report was discouraging from the first page
She was alarmed by what she heard
